text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition on its own is not evidence. All-women panels occur routinely by chance in many departments, and no tribunal or ombudsman treats the selectors' sex as probative. Raising it makes you look like you're reasoning backwards from the outcome, and it will overshadow your genuinely stronger point.

That stronger point is procedural: you were shortlisted, interviewed twice, and have been denied written reasons for two weeks. Chase that — escalate to the HR director or dean, citing the university's own recruitment policy and any statutory right to feedback. Ask what criteria were weighted and how.

Also consider that "industry experience" may have been a stated priority, and that interview performance and teaching-fit can legitimately outrank publication counts.
